headline: School Proves Housing Insecurity Doesn't Mean Missing Class
meta_description: Scholarship Prep South Bay kept all 54 homeless students engaged in school last year through community partnerships providing food and transportation.
summary_short: A Los Angeles school achieved perfect attendance rates among its 54 homeless students by leveraging 50+ community partnerships for essential support.
body:
Scholarship Prep South Bay in Los Angeles proved that homelessness doesn't have to mean dropping out of school. Last year, the school had 54 students experiencing homelessness, and none of them were chronically absent.

The achievement rests on the school's extensive community network. With more than 50 partnerships in place, the institution provides critical support that removes barriers to daily attendance—including food assistance and transportation. These services address some of the most pressing obstacles facing homeless youth, who often struggle simply to get to school or go through the day without hunger.

The success story offers a quiet rebuttal to the assumption that stable housing is a prerequisite for educational engagement. When schools address the concrete needs of their most vulnerable students, consistent attendance becomes possible.

Zero chronically absent students despite housing insecurity
50+ community partnerships providing food and transportation
